screening_decisions.reason: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot of intracervical nitroprusside gel given immediately prior to IUD insertion; primary outcome was patient-reported insertion pain (VAS).
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of ibuprofen 800 mg 30–45 minutes pre-insertion; self-reported pain measured by VAS during IUD insertion.
Randomized trial (full vs emptied bladder) assessing provider ease and women’s pain scores during IUC insertion; pain outcomes included.

Randomized, open-label parallel-group trial comparing intracervical 2% lidocaine injection vs oral NSAID before LNG-IUS insertion; patient-reported pain at insertion and post-insertion time points measured.
Double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT of 800 mg ibuprofen 45 minutes prior to LNG-IUS insertion; pain at tenaculum placement and insertion measured.
Double-blind, multicenter RCT of 400 µg vaginal misoprostol vs placebo 3 h prior to IUD insertion; included insertion pain outcomes.
Randomized, double-blind trial of 400 µg buccal misoprostol vs placebo 90 min prior to IUD insertion in nulliparous women; multiple self-reported pain time points (including tenaculum and insertion).
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of sublingual misoprostol 3 h prior to repeat LNG-IUS insertion; included pain outcomes.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled prophylactic ibuprofen (400 mg) trial in first-time IUD users; immediate post-insertion pain measured via VAS.
Single-blind RCT of sublingual misoprostol + diclofenac vs diclofenac alone 1 h pre-insertion in women without prior vaginal delivery; insertion-related pain outcomes included.
Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study of ibuprofen 600 mg given pre- and post-insertion; pain assessed during insertion and up to 4–6 hours post (within protocol window).
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial comparing oral tramadol, naproxen, and placebo 1 h before IUD insertion; insertion pain measured (VAS).
Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of 400 µg buccal misoprostol vs placebo before IUD insertion in nulliparous women; provider ease and patient pain measured.
Randomized, double-blind clinical trial of intracervical 2% lidocaine gel vs placebo with VAS pain ratings at multiple insertion-related time points.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot of 0.5 mg vaginal nitroglycerin gel 30 min prior to LNG-IUS placement; insertion pain assessed (VAS).
Randomized trial of 1% lidocaine paracervical block vs no anesthetic; reported VAS pain at tenaculum placement, during insertion, and 5 min post-procedure.
Randomized, double-blind controlled trial of 2% lidocaine gel vs lubricant vs no intervention applied to the cervical canal; insertion pain measured (VAS).
Randomized, double-blind pilot comparing intrauterine 2% lidocaine vs normal saline infused 3 min before IUD insertion; pain assessed at tenaculum and during insertion.
Randomized controlled trial of sublingual misoprostol + diclofenac vs diclofenac alone 1 h before insertion in nulliparous women; insertion pain (VAS) reported.
Randomized, double-blind clinical trial of 400 µg vaginal misoprostol 4 h before insertion in nulligravidas; insertion pain reduced; outcomes within scope.
Randomized, placebo-controlled aromatherapy (lavender inhalation) vs placebo 30 min pre-insertion; anxiety and IUD insertion pain (VAS) measured.
Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of self-administered misoprostol vs placebo 3–4 h pre-insertion in nulliparous women; perceived pain during insertion measured.
Randomized, placebo-controlled phase II trial of a novel topical lidocaine formulation applied to portio/cervix/uterus; insertion pain (VAS) significantly reduced.

Prospective, single-blinded, controlled study of paracervical 1% lidocaine vs placebo vs no treatment; self-reported pain at tenaculum, insertion, and 5 min post included. Randomization not stated—include at abstract screening with uncertainty noted.
Randomized clinical trial of misoprostol vs placebo prior to IUD insertion in nulliparous women; primary outcome: pain at insertion (VAS).
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (abstract) of self-administered 2% lidocaine vaginal gel 5 min pre-insertion; pain at insertion primary outcome.
Not an RCT; descriptive experience/opinion on intracervical anesthesia technique, no randomized comparison of pain outcomes.
Prospective cohort (observational) comparing pain by parity; no randomized intervention to prevent insertion-related pain.
Qualitative study of non-users’ perceptions; not an interventional RCT on insertion-related pain.
Narrative/practical review; not a randomized controlled trial.
Methodological guidance (GRADE); not about IUD insertion pain interventions and not an RCT.
Committee opinion on adolescents and LARC; not an RCT of pain interventions at IUD insertion.
Review of pain management strategies; secondary research; not a primary RCT.
Review of misoprostol in gynecology; not a randomized trial of IUD insertion pain.
Observational evaluation of expected vs actual pain; no randomized analgesic intervention.
Methodological GRADE guidance; not an RCT of IUD insertion pain.
Predictive study of difficult/painful insertion; no interventional RCT to reduce pain.
Evidence-based review; not a primary randomized trial.
Systematic review of intrauterine anesthesia across procedures; not a primary IUD insertion RCT.
Observational clinic study on pre-analgesia and anxiety; not randomized.
Review on adolescent contraception; not an RCT of insertion pain interventions.
Meta-analysis of analgesic options; not a primary RCT.
RCT on cervical ripening before surgical termination (not IUD insertion); wrong procedure/population for this review.
Clinician survey on insertion techniques; not a randomized controlled trial.
Methodology paper for a prospective meta-analysis; not reporting an individual RCT’s outcomes.
Commentary/editorial arguing against misoprostol use; not a randomized trial.
Randomized trial of post-insertion analgesic (meptazinol) to treat pain after insertion; outside scope focused on preventing insertion-related pain.
Randomized clinical trial of lavender aromatherapy vs placebo vs control; insertion pain (VAS) compared across groups.
Technique description for paracervical block; not a randomized trial.
Cochrane review of NSAIDs for IUD-associated bleeding/pain; secondary research, not a primary RCT.
